neighbours.label: The corrective step in conditional advice — 'if it is too dry, add more…', 'you can raise the humidity by…', 'you can help by expanding it' — strongest when the fix is to add or increase something. Describing the same condition with no fix, or an increase that is merely reported, stays quiet.
fire: If the batter looks too stiff, pour in a splash more milk.
If the air in the nursery is too dry, you can boost the moisture with a bowl of water near the heater.
This entry is only an outline. You can help by adding to it.
If the paint seems too thick, thin it with a few more drops of water.
When the compost heap dries out, sprinkle it with the hose until it is damp again.
If the stew tastes bland, add another pinch of salt and a little more pepper.
If the tyres feel soft, pump in more air until they are firm.
Not a member yet? Join today and get extra discounts on every order.
quiet: The batter looked too stiff, and the cake came out heavy.
The air in the nursery was too dry all winter, and the baby slept badly.
This entry was only an outline when the editors first saw it.
The paint seemed too thick, and the brush left ridges on the wall.
Rainfall increased over the weekend, and the compost heap stayed damp.
The stew tasted bland, and nobody asked for a second bowl.
Prices rose again in March, and the tyres cost more than last year.
Membership grew by a third last year, mostly through word of mouth.

short: the fix in 'if too X, add…' advice
notes: Card: ' humidity' (increase the humidity), ' sprinkle', ' gain', 'Join', ' more' (add more), ' expanding' (Wikipedia stub notices). Probes: add more water 0.76, raise the humidity 0.90, stir in another spoonful 0.67, help by expanding 0.66, extra compost 0.34; fixes that reduce: lower the humidity 0.41, remove some broth 0.41, trimming 0.21, let it rest 0.24; plain description 0.01. So reducing fixes also fire somewhat; the near misses here are non-advice sentences, and the add-versus-reduce contrast is not tested.
